mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the effect reverses for three consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes either wage inflation or policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent in two consecutive cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo MA and CPIAUCSL > 12mo MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 1% in both real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and retail sales (HOUST) signals a demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 1% AND HOUST monthly change > 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market strength, which supports earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 50,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-average payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of less than -0.2% combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and UNRATE meet the specified conditions.
